outcome: functional implications (self-care, interpersonal interactions and relationships, domestic life)
cohort: 96 women older than 18 years who had undergone cesarean section with a Pfannenstiel incision 6-36 months prior to the study.
finding: Cesarean section skin scars were found to lead to dissatisfaction and functional impairments, particularly affecting self-care and interpersonal interactions and relationships, thereby impacting women's quality of life.
mod_finding: Cesarean section scars were found to cause dissatisfaction and functional impairments, impacting women's quality of life.
